issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a Developer instance method named attend(course:), but the solution's Developer implementation defines a method named participateIn(course:). Additionally, the solution's Client calls myself.attend(course:), creating a mismatch inside the solution itself. This discrepancy in the method name/signature will confuse students and prevents the provided Client code from compiling or running as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name/signature consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (preferred to match the problem statement and template) or update the template/problem to use participateIn(course:). Also ensure Client, template stubs, and solution all use the exact same method name and parameter list so the code compiles and students can follow the intended exercise.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Developer instance method named attend(course:), but the solution implements this behavior under the different identifier participateIn(course:). This naming divergence (attend vs. participateIn) refers to the same conceptual operation (a developer attending/participating in a course) and creates a mapping confusion for students: they will look for attend(course:) as described in the exercise and in the template, but the solution uses a different name.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution method participateIn(course:) to attend(course:) (or alternatively rename the template and problem to use participateIn) so the exercise description, starter code, and solution reference the same identifier. Also ensure Client calls the same method name.
